build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 61: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 62's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 3-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 61's value table (side 4's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 61's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$0026, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$0015, channel 2's script at +$001F and 0 for channel 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 2 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 2, frame 1 then 3. One pass takes 5 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 3 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 6, frame 3 then 17, frame 3 then 4. One pass takes 27 steps.

Channel 2's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 2 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 2 then 15, frame 4 then 20. One pass takes 35 steps.

Picture 61's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $03 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 33 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 61, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1 and 2: a run count of 0 to start, then 20 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 35 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 61, named by channel 1's entry 1 and channel 2's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 3 of picture 61, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 8 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 38 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 61, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entry 2: a run count of 0 to start, then 18 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 52 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 9. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 61's own packed bytes decode to, the 1,029th byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
